rationale: Anchored to the Management section; tests the critical principle that force-feeding converts transient difficulties into chronic aversive feeding disorders.
Anchored to the Clinical Presentation section; tests the key classification concept that feeding problems span organic, behavioural, and mixed categories.
Anchored to the Clinical Presentation block; targets the high-yield distinction between cyanotic and pallid breath-holding spells which is a frequent exam and clinical error.
Anchored to the Management block; tests whether students know that parental reassurance — not pharmacotherapy — is the cornerstone of management for uncomplicated breath-holding spells.
Anchored to the Pathophysiology block; tests the pica-iron deficiency vicious cycle — a key factual trap highlighted in the PE known-traps brief.
Anchored to the Diagnosis and Investigation block; applies knowledge of pica to a clinical scenario requiring investigation of lead exposure.
Anchored to the Clinical Presentation and Classification block; tests the precise definitions of primary vs secondary enuresis and the age threshold — a key factual trap.
Anchored to the Management block; tests that non-pharmacological therapies — specifically the enuresis alarm — are first-line before pharmacotherapy in uncomplicated primary nocturnal enuresis.
